text: Dr. Amara Osei reviews the disappointing hardware results and asks the question the team's plan skipped entirely.
We validated against an ideal simulator, then jumped straight to real hardware -- what did we actually expect to happen in between?
She runs the identical circuit through FakeBrisbane, a simulator noise-modeled on ibm_brisbane's own real calibration data -- without spending any more real quantum time.
The noise-modeled simulation reproduces the real hardware's flattened results closely -- far closer than the ideal simulator ever did.
Strong evidence the gap is uncompensated hardware noise, not a flaw in the algorithm. Diagnosed -- but not yet fixed.
